key_insight: ContiLNN adds bidirectional liquid-neural cross-slice modeling to a 2D restoration backbone so medical images can use neighboring-slice context while staying robust to irregular slice spacing.
clinical_relevance: This could improve CT, MRI, and PET image restoration quality in settings where slice sampling is uneven, potentially yielding clearer images for downstream interpretation.
method: Bi-CfC modules model cross-slice continuity in both directions without ODE solving.
Slice-index intervals and local features modulate propagation gates to adapt to sampling gaps.
Reference-guided consistency and frozen-backbone distillation help preserve anatomical variation and in-plane detail.
evidence_signal: Across five seeds, ContiLNN improved mean PSNR over Restore-RWKV on CT denoising, MRI super-resolution, and reduced-count PET restoration, with lower RMSE on all three tasks; profiling also showed lower latency and GPU memory than Bi-GRU.
watch_item: Some results are reported descriptively for a single held-out CT patient, so broader validation and real-world robustness testing are still needed.
paper_title: ContiLNN: Mitigating Slice Sampling Discontinuity with Liquid Neural Networks for Medical Image Restoration
